scope: M2 immutable workspace and Pi Session base lineage from claim through checkpoint

findings: P1: a Turn had no immutable workspace or Pi Session input checkpoint, so retry or restore could observe a different base
P1: parentRevisionId was an opaque snapshot value without existence, scope or Session verification
resolution: WorkspaceAgent journal schema v2 stores the latest workspace head and each Session head, then freezes both receipts in the same transaction that claims a Turn
Dispatcher, Product Runtime, Trusted Pi execution/native adapters and Revision manifest carry the exact frozen base
Trusted Pi genesis requires no input Session; restore requires bytes whose SHA-256 equals the frozen Session receipt
Revision commit reads and validates every claimed base manifest and blob before freezing output, including tenant/project/workspace/generation and Session ownership
durable state rejects rolled-back heads, forged receipts and cross-Session base references before execution

coverage: Product Runtime idempotency digest includes the base
R2 base manifest and blob existence, digest, scope and Session checks
legacy v1 state migration on the next mutation
head rollback, forged receipt and cross-Session state corruption
macOS one-shot file helper boundary without an unbounded test subprocess

productPlatform: head selection, claim-time freezing, receipt validation, Runtime routing and Revision authority are platform functions
project Pi receives only the verified Session bytes selected by the platform and cannot choose or rewrite base receipts
notAccepted: real Workspace canonical archive and restore
real Pi Session restore in a built cloud image
cloud Turn execution or M2 completion
